chunks: From him, from one of his companions, from Ziyad Al-Qindy, from Durust Bin Abu Mansour, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is an Angel, whose span from his ear lobe to his shoulder is the distance a bird travels in five hundred years.
ai.seo_question: What is the physical size of an angel according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the vast physical dimensions of the angels, using the metaphor of a bird's flight over five hundred years to illustrate the distance from an angel's earlobe to its shoulder. In Shia scholarly tradition, this description underscores the tangible reality of the celestial realm and the majesty of Allah's creation, serving as a reminder of the grandeur associated with the Day of Judgment. It reflects the belief in the physicality of angels as distinct entities within the cosmic order.

en.hubeali: H 14853 – From him, from one of his companions, from Ziyad Al-Qindy, from Durust Bin Abu Mansour, from a man, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws having said that:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has an Angel, whose span between his ear lobe to his shoulder is of five hundred years of the travel distance of a bird’.
en.sarwar: 406. From him, from one of his companions, from Ziyad Al-Qindy, from Durust Bin Abu Mansour, from a man, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) having said that:
‘Allah (azwj) has an Angel, whose span between his ear lobe to his shoulder is of five hundred years of the travel distance of a bird’.
